_comment: TEMPLATE for the Copilot CLI, which reads %USERPROFILE%\.copilot\mcp-config.json. It cannot use ${input:...} - it can only pass --env KEY=VALUE - and its folder is readable by another group on Windows, so a password here would not be private. Instead the server entry names a connection, and sap-arc1-launcher.ps1 resolves the password from Windows Credential Manager at start. Copy this block into the arc-1 entry of your mcp-config.json; keep your own policy variables.
_rule: No SAP_PASSWORD in env. URL, client, user and language come from arc1-connections.json, so a second logon needs no edit here at all.
_command: The interpreter is named by absolute path on purpose. A bare "powershell" only resolves while System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0 is on PATH, and a sandboxed or trimmed parent environment does not have it - the server then fails to start and the tools simply never appear.
